events.system:
P = propan-1-ol
P --[SOCl₂, pyridine]--> Q
Q --[Zn, H⁺]--> R
R --[Br₂, hν]--> S
Q --[Mg, dry ether]--> T
Q --[alc. KOH, heat]--> U
events.hidden_link: P to Q is a substitution to form an alkyl chloride. Q to R is a reduction to an alkane. R to S is a free radical halogenation, which is highly regioselective for the more substituted carbon. Q to T forms a Grignard reagent. Q to U is an elimination reaction to form an alkene.
events.route: 1. P (propan-1-ol) reacts with SOCl2 to give Q (1-chloropropane). 2. Q is reduced by Zn/H+ to give R (propane). 3. Radical bromination of R yields S (2-bromopropane) as the major product due to the greater stability of the secondary radical. 4. Q reacts with Mg in dry ether to form T (propylmagnesium chloride). 5. Q undergoes E2 elimination with alc. KOH to form U (propene).
events.student_must_notice: The regioselectivity in the formation of S (radical bromination favors the secondary carbon, not the primary) and the elimination of Q to form U.
events.trap: Assuming S is 1-bromopropane (ignoring radical stability) or misidentifying the functional groups and hybridisation states in U.

members.name: granite-4.2-8b
members.working: P = propan-1-ol. SOCl2 with pyridine converts primary alcohol to chloroalkane Q = chloropropane (1-chloropropane). Zn/H+ reduces C-Cl to alkane R = propane. Br2 hv monobromination of alkane gives bromoalkane with anti addition? For propane, bromination gives 1-bromopropane (primary) and 2-bromopropane (secondary) as major? Typically bromination of alkanes via radical mechanism favors secondary > primary, so major S = 2-bromopropane. So (A) true. Q -- Mg dry ether gives Grignard T = propylmagnesium bromide. Q -- alc KOH heat eliminates HCl to give alkene U = propene (CH2=CHCH3). Propene decolorises bromine water (addition) so (B) true. Propene has one sp2 carbon (the double bond carbon) actually both carbons in double bond are sp2, so two sp2 carbons? In propene CH2=CHCH3, the two carbons in double bond are sp2, the terminal CH3 carbon is sp3. So three carbons total, two sp2? Wait: CH2=CH-CH3: carbon 1 (CH2) sp2, carbon 2 (CH) sp2, carbon 3 (CH3) sp3. So two sp2 carbons, not three. So (C) false. Compound S (2-bromopropane) has no stereocentre because CHBrCH2CH3? 2-bromopropane is CH3-CH(Br)-CH3, that carbon is attached to two CH3 groups, Br, H -> could be chiral? CH(Br) with two CH3 groups identical? Actually CH3-CH(Br)-CH3 has two identical CH3 groups, so not chiral. So (D) false. Thus correct options: A and B. However check (A) major product S formed upon monobromination of R (propane) is 2-bromopropane? Radical bromination favors secondary > primary, so major is 2-bromopropane. So A true. B true. So answer AB.

Excess NH3 substitutes both Cl in R to give primary amines in U. HNO2 converts one primary amine in U to OH, giving V.

members.working: P = benzene-1,2-dicarboxylic acid (two COOH groups para? actually 1,2). (i) LiAlH4 reduces carboxylic acids to alcohols: P -> benzene-1,2-diol (Q). (ii) H2O workup gives Q = 1,2-benzenedicarboxylic acid reduced? Actually LiAlH4 reduces both COOH to CH2OH? Wait LiAlH4 reduces carboxylic acid to primary alcohol: -COOH -> -CH2OH. So Q = benzene-1,2-diol (1,2-benzenedicarboxylic acid reduced to 1,2-benzenedicarboxylic acid? No, reduction of dicarboxylic acid gives diol? Actually -COOH -> -CH2OH, so Q = 1,2-benzenedicarboxylic acid? No, becomes 1,2-benzenedicarboxylic acid? Let's assume Q = 1,2-benzenedicarboxylic acid? Better: P = HOOC-C6H4-COOH (1,2). LiAlH4 reduces both COOH to CH2OH giving HOCH2-C6H4-CH2OH (1,2-benzenediol). Then SOCl2 converts OH to Cl: R = benzene-1,2-dichloride (Cl-C6H4-Cl). NaCN in DMSO does nucleophilic substitution? Cl replaced by CN giving benzene-1,2-dicyano (S). KMnO4, H+, heat oxidizes diol? Q (diol) oxidized to dicarboxylic acid? Actually diol 1,2-benzenediol oxidized to 1,2-benzenedicarboxylic acid (T). R (dichloride) with NaCN gives dicyano (S). R with NH3 excess gives amide formation: Cl replaced by CONH2 giving benzene-1,2-dicarboxamide (U). U with NaNO2/HCl gives diazonium salt which eliminates to give benzene-1,2-dione? Actually amide diazotization then loss of N2 gives carboxylic acid? Might give benzene-1,2-dicarboxylic acid? V likely benzene-1,2-dione (two carbonyls). Evaluate statements: (A) T is dicarboxylic acid, no CO2 effervescence with NaHCO3 (no acidic COOH? dicarboxylic acid reacts with NaHCO3 to produce CO2? Carboxylic acid + NaHCO3 gives CO2? Yes, acid + bicarbonate releases CO2. So T would produce effervescence. Likely true. (B) S = 1,2-dicyano benzene. Each CN has sp hybridized carbon? The carbon in CN is sp hybridized (trigonal planar? Actually nitrile carbon is sp hybridized). So exactly one sp carbon? Both carbons of CN are sp hybridized? The carbon in CN is sp hybridized, the attached carbon (benzene carbon) is sp2. So S has two nitrile groups -> two sp carbons. So statement B false. (C) U = dicarboxamide. Carbylamine test positive for primary amine? Amide gives negative. So U does not give positive carbylamine test. Statement C true. (D) V = benzene-1,2-dione (two carbonyls). Degree of unsaturation: benzene ring (4) + two C=O (each 1) = 6? Actually benzene ring contributes 4 (3 double bonds equivalent? Degree unsaturation = 4 for benzene (3 double bonds + 1 ring = 4). Each carbonyl adds 1 (C=O). So total 6. But V might have ring plus two carbonyls = 6. Statement D says 5, false. So correct: A and C. Return AC.

members.name: glm-5.3-flash
members.working: P = phthalic acid. (i) LiAlH4 reduces both COOH to CH2OH → Q = benzene-1,2-dimethanol (phthalyl alcohol). Q + SOCl2/pyridine → R = 1,2-bis(chloromethyl)benzene. R + NaCN (SN2) → S = o-C6H4(CH2CN)2, containing two sp-hybridised nitrile carbons, so (B) is false. Q oxidized with hot KMnO4/H+ → T = phthalic acid, which effervesces CO2 with NaHCO3, so (A) is true. R + excess NH3 → U = o-xylylenediamine, a primary diamine, which DOES give the carbylamine test, so (C) is false. U + NaNO2/dil. HCl: primary aliphatic amines give unstable diazonium ions that hydrolyze to alcohols, so V = benzene-1,2-dimethanol (or mixture of alcohols), DoU = 4 (benzene ring), not 5, so (D) is false. Only (A) is correct.

members.name: minimax-m3
members.working: P = phthalic acid. LiAlH4 → Q = 1,2-bis(hydroxymethyl)benzene. SOCl2 → R = 1,2-bis(chloromethyl)benzene. NaCN → S = 1,2-bis(cyanomethyl)benzene (has 2 sp carbons, not 1, so B wrong). KMnO4 → T = phthalic acid (carboxylic acid, gives CO2 with NaHCO3, so A correct). NH3 → U = 1,2-bis(aminomethyl)benzene (primary amine, gives positive carbylamine test, so C wrong). NaNO2/HCl → V = 1,2-bis(hydroxymethyl)benzene, C8H10O2, DoU = (2*8+2-10)/2 = 4, not 5, so D wrong.
